text.p: Big-serving Croat Goran Ivanisevic threw Swede Mikael Tillstrom out of the Grand Slam Cup with of subtlety of a night-club bouncer and grabbed a pay cheque of $262,500.
The defending champion put on a powerful display of aggressive serving to clinch a 6-4 6-2 victory in just 55 minutes in the first-round of the most lucrative tournament in tennis.
Munich's indoor Olympic arena has witnessed some graceful sporting performances over the years, notably from gymnast Olga Korbut at the 1972 Games. This was not one of them, however.
There were very few rallies on the fast surface as both players hammered in serves of up to 200 kph. Ivanisevic can play some subtle tennis but he rarely needed to against the Swede.
This was a performance of power, punch and little panache from the Croat, wearing his long hair tied up at the front.
The only real drama in the first set came in the seventh game when Ivanisevic had a break point.
Tillstrom's volley at the net clearly landed out of court but was called in. Ivanisevic spent a minute arguing with the umpire after watching a replay on the television screen above the court.
The Croat eventually cooled down and managed a break in the game and went on to clinch the set after 31 minutes after the best rally of the match during which he hit a half-volley through his legs.
That was it in entertainment terms.

Another break early in the second set steered the Croat to the quarter-finals where he will shooting for a cheque of $431,250. Ivanisevic has already earned $2.8 million in four appearances at the event.
